Testing a weighted combination with the pooled_meta_model handle (w1) on the full pool to see if a meta‑model based weighting can beat the current median baseline given the strong trend and moderate ranking stability.
Test trimmed_mean on the full pool to see if trimming outliers improves performance in this trend‑dominated, low‑seasonality series.
I will test a weighted combination on the smaller, more focused pool1, hoping that removing some noisy models improves performance.
Test a simple mean over all models to see if averaging improves over trimmed mean, motivated by high predictability and trend dominance.
trend_dominated series suggests weighted combination with a broader pool; try weighted on pool2 with inverse_error weights.
try a robust DBA weighting on the full model pool to see if iterative reweighting improves over trimmed mean, motivated by high predictability and trend dominance.
Using the trend‑dominated, highly predictable series, test a weighted combination on the larger pool3 to see if more models help the inverse‑error weighting.
Test a simple median over a small, trend‑focused pool (pool1) to see if a robust estimator improves on trimmed mean for a trend‑dominated series.
test a trimmed‑mean on the smaller pool2 to reduce variance while keeping weighted‑style robustness for this trend‑dominated series.
Test a simple mean over a smaller, high‑performing pool (pool1) to see if averaging only the top models beats the trimmed mean baseline, given the strong trend and high predictability.

decision.justification: Selected 'trimmed_mean' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.966. Series context: trend strength 0.8983 and seasonal strength 0.0; model ranking is moderate across windows (Kendall tau 0.446); 3 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 4.893.
